subtitles.text: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree, Minecraft edition. LeetCode two ninety seven, a hard one.
We have a tree built from blocks, and we must save it as one line of text.
Then load that text back into the exact same tree.
First idea. Write just the values, in preorder. The node, then its left side, then its right side.
Our tree becomes five, eight, two, seven.
But this tree also reads five, eight, two, seven. And so does this one.
Same text, three different builds. The shape is lost.
Here's the trick. Whenever a child is missing, we write a hash mark, like a barrier block.
The markers record the shape, so one text can only describe one tree.
Let's save it. We walk in preorder, and each step fills the next slot.
Five goes in. Then left, eight. Eight has no children, so a pair of barriers.
Back up to two. Its left is seven, a leaf, so another pair.
Two has no right child. One last barrier, and the save is done.
Five, eight, hash, hash, two, seven, hash, hash, hash.
Now we clear the build, and load it back, reading the slots in the same order.
Five is the root. Eight goes left. A pair of barriers closes it, so we climb back up.
Two goes right, seven on its left, and the last barriers close every branch.
Advancement made. The tree is back, exactly as it was.
Each node is written once and read once, so both directions are linear.
The text holds n values and n plus one markers. Linear space too.
Two short functions. One walks and writes, the other reads and builds, in the same order.
Mark the empty spots, and any tree survives the trip.
